name: hold-cmd-q-panel
description: The restyled 'Hold ⌘Q to Quit' HUD (overlay design language, direction D/brand look): a paper card with keycaps for the shortcut. confirmToQuitEnabled is staged true so the very first Cmd+Q shows the panel. key_delay_ms is 400 - proven safe by settings-confirm-quit-takes-effect.json's own first chord - well under the ~500ms mark where ConfirmQuitPanelController's targetDate/kTimeDeltaFuzzFactor math commits to quitting, so this is a tap the panel treats as cancelled: the key comes up, the panel stays fully visible for about another second, then fades. mid_at_ms lands after the release and well before that fade starts, so the capture is the panel at rest rather than mid-animation. ax_window_count at the end is the assertion that the release actually beat the quit - a build that committed anyway would leave no window to count.

actions.note: gate: the startup tab committed, so the browser window is up before Cmd+Q is sent
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
the panel: paper surface, ink, and the shortcut as keycaps followed by 'to Quit'. Released at 400ms, safely under the ~500ms commit mark, so the panel dismisses instead of the app quitting
let the panel's fade-out finish before the run ends

assertions.desc: the browser window is still there - the release beat the quit. The HUD itself is far below min_area, so it cannot pad this count

assertions.label: confirm-to-quit-is-armed
assertions.note: the gate this scenario is about was actually on for this launch, so the panel that appeared is the confirm-to-quit HUD and not some other window
